high_level_description: Wordless Aubusson tapestry illustration of a modern lissière keeping a richly patterned wool hanging inside a private workshop while deliberately placing one separate, drastically simplified woven swatch in an outward-facing public niche, where a visitor can see only that small selection; flat interlocked wool forms, no text or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: An Aubusson workshop occupies the left two-thirds of a tall cutaway scene, with lime-plastered walls, a pale timber floor, a high north-facing window, and cool daylight. A solid cream partition separates it from a simple stone public forecourt on the right; one shallow presentation niche opens toward the forecourt while the rich workshop interior remains outside a direct exterior sightline. No inscription, letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow, diagram, badge, lock, bars, cage, surveillance device, religious emblem, heraldry, or national symbol appears anywhere.

elements.desc: Large freestanding oak display rack entirely inside the workshop, carrying one uncut wool hanging dense with interlocking indigo branches, madder leaves, ochre tools, cream vessels, and irregular green birds. Near the upper-right corner sits a distinctive three-leaf sprig in blue, red, and cream; the remaining field contains many unrelated motifs and colors.

Adult Aubusson lissière inside the workshop, light-brown skin, dark curly hair tied back, indigo work smock over a cream shirt, ochre trousers, and flat brown shoes. With a calm concentrated expression, she slides one separate woven square into the presentation niche using her right hand; her left hand remains beside the private hanging.

Small outward-facing oak display frame on the public side of the niche, receiving one separate palm-sized woven square. The square reproduces only the distinctive blue, red, and cream three-leaf sprig from the large hanging on otherwise empty undyed wool; it contains none of the birds, vessels, tools, branches, or additional colors.

Adult public visitor standing in the forecourt, dark skin, close-cropped black hair, charcoal jacket, muted blue trousers, and brown shoes. Their neutral attentive gaze rests on the tiny outward-facing swatch at eye level. The solid partition blocks every direct line of sight toward the large tapestry and the rest of the workshop.
